summary: Develop practical systems thinking skills for complex projects using causal maps, system dynamics, and risk interventions. Enrol with TrainingCred.
lede: Systems thinking in project management examines how dependencies, feedback and stakeholder decisions interact to shape delivery outcomes. For project and programme managers, PMO leads and project controls specialists, the training focuses on diagnosing recurring delivery problems that schedule and cost reports alone may not explain. Learners practise mapping stakeholders and dependencies, building causal loop diagrams, testing delivery scenarios, and prioritising interventions to create a systems-oriented performance dashboard and action roadmap.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who must coordinate interconnected work, interpret project signals, and make decisions when simple task management cannot explain the outcome.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working knowledge of project management, project lifecycle stages, risk registers, schedules, stakeholder engagement, and basic performance reporting. Prior exposure to the PMI PMBOK Guide or ISO 21502 is useful but not required. No programming is required. You should bring a current or representative project scenario for application exercises where confidentiality permits. Advanced concept depth: Systems dynamics, causal modelling, and AI-assisted analysis are taught primarily at operational application and conceptual modelling level. The course does not aim to produce production-grade simulation software or enterprise implementation architecture.
